plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin DE (Salmon counts)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is one gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv) produced by Salmon, plus a 12x2 sample table (metadata.csv) giving condition for 6 atopic-dermatitis lesional skin samples and 6 controls, unpaired, single batch, human. The research question is purely which genes differ between the two conditions, so the plan stops at differential expression and its report — no enrichment, no deconvolution, no unasked scope.

The one real methodological hazard is stated in the profile itself: the table came from Salmon but the per-sample quant.sf files and any average-transcript-length table were not delivered, and the record does not say whether a length correction (lengthScaledTPM / scaledTPM) was applied. A quantifier name alone does not establish the import state. There is no way to recover the offset from a gene-level table, and tximport must not be run on one. The plan therefore fits the negative-binomial model on the counts exactly as delivered, with no length offset, checks whether the values are integer or fractional (rounding only if fractional, and saying so), and requires the report to state that the length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can appear as differential expression. T1S0 exists to record that determination explicitly rather than let it be assumed downstream.

T1S1 is design-blind sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) so that an outlier or an unexpected structure is seen before any test is fitted; with a single batch, PCA colouring is by condition and library size. T1S2 fits DESeq2 with an explicitly set reference level (control as denominator, so a positive log2 fold change means higher in AD lesional), a minimal pre-filter of >=10 counts in >=6 samples, median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, the Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the reported effect, independent filtering on, and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 — the alpha passed to results() being the same alpha the report uses. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts, so those NAs must be reported separately from the independent-filter NAs. T1S3 runs edgeR quasi-likelihood on the identical filtered matrix and design as a robustness check; the two methods are the second method of each other at this replicate level. T1S4 assembles the report: shrunken and unshrunken effects side by side, MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set, and a full reproducibility record. Twelve samples of 12,000 genes is a tiny matrix, so resources are small throughout.

median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
~ condition with explicit reference level control, counts as delivered without length offset
DE report with MA plot, dispersion plot, method overlap, reproducibility record

acceptance_criteria: Method, package versions, design, contrast, thresholds, n tested and n DE appear before the gene tables.
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram all present, each with an interpretation sentence.
Gene table carries unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold change plus lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value, shrinkage estimator named.
DESeq2/edgeR intersection reported as the high-confidence set; single-method calls listed separately, not merged into a union.
The lost length offset and its consequence for isoform-usage confounding is stated as a limitation, together with the specific input that would resolve it.
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, package versions, seed) stored with the results.
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit.
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR as the result.
Do not add enrichment, pathway, or gene-set analysis — the research question does not ask for it.
Do not state or imply that the counts were length-corrected, and do not state that they were not; state that the import state is unknown and what was assumed.
caveats: Interpretation of individual genes should not outrun a 6-vs-6 unpaired design; effects near the padj boundary are provisional.

Skin biopsies vary in cellular composition between lesional and control tissue, so a gene-level difference may reflect a shift in cell-type proportion rather than per-cell regulation. This is not testable from bulk counts alone and should be flagged, not resolved.

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as a whole; the reporting settings and claims returned by the procedure are carried verbatim.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
~ condition with explicit reference level control, counts as delivered without length offset
DE report with MA plot, dispersion plot, method overlap, reproducibility record

violations.message: Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate with independent filtering is not a permitted method for filter_low_counts in this situation.
permitted: Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples

warnings.message: Parameter test = QLF differs from the sourced default Wald (doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8).
